title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the proof of 'Théorème 3', begun on the previous page. Let K be finitely generated over Q. Let X be geometrically connected and embeddable in a semi-abelian variety G, meaning an extension of an abelian variety by a torus; the main case is an elementary Artin neighbourhood whose fibres are not P^1 or A^1. The theorem says two canonical maps are injective. The first, (*), sends X(K) to π1(X̄)-conjugacy classes of sections of the fundamental extension 1→π1(X̄)→π1(X)→Gal(K̄/K)→1. The second, (**), sends X(K) to conjugacy classes of sections of its abelianization by H1(X̄). This is the injectivity half of the section conjecture.

Step 1 (reduction). The map (*) factors through (**), so it suffices to prove (**) injective. Sections of the abelianized extension, up to conjugacy, form a torsor under H^1(K, H1(X̄)). Map X into G by an Albanese-type morphism. The difference of the classes of two points then becomes the Kummer-type class of their difference in G. This reduces the problem to X = G, where the map is a group homomorphism (16): G(K) = H^0(K,G) → H^1(K, H1(Ḡ)), with H1(Ḡ) = T(G) = lim_n nG the full (all-n) Tate module.

Step 2 (Kummer theory). For each n ≥ 1 there is an exact sequence 0 → nG → G --n--> G → 0, using that multiplication by n is étale-surjective in characteristic 0. It gives 0 → G(K)/n → H^1(K, nG) → nH^1(K,G) → 0. Since inverse limits are left exact, this yields 0 → lim G(K)/n → lim H^1(K, nG).

Step 3 (compatibility). Compose (16) with the natural map H^1(K, T(G)) → lim H^1(K, nG). The result is the Kummer map G(K) → lim G(K)/n → lim H^1(K, nG). This is the standard compatibility of the 'section class' of a point with its Kummer class.

Step 4 (finished on the next page). The kernel is ∩_n nG(K), the infinitely divisible elements. A Mordell–Weil type finiteness argument shows these are trivial, so (16) is injective.

The next-page remark adds two points. Using only one ℓ (the Z_ℓ Tate module) does not suffice: translation by a K-rational point of order p ≠ ℓ gives a counterexample. The result is equivalent to the triviality of the T∞(G)-torsor obtained from x by pulling back multiplication by n.
errors: Final step (next page): 'Mordell–Weil gives G(K) finitely generated' is false when G has a torus part. For example G_m(K) = K^* is not finitely generated even for K = Q. The conclusion ∩ nG(K) = 0 still holds, by a different argument. A(K) is finitely generated (Lang–Néron), so divisible elements map to 0 in A(K). A torsion argument (A(K)_tors has finite exponent m) then puts such an element in T(K) and makes it divisible there. Finally, T(K) has no nontrivial divisible elements: it embeds in (L^*)^r, and L^* is the product of a finite group and a free abelian group.
Line 'H^0(K) → lim H^0(K,G)_n' should read H^0(K,G).

The reduction to X = G is only sketched. The Albanese map needs a base point or must be taken into the Albanese torsor. It also needs to be injective on X(K), or at least to separate the points being compared. For X embedded in G this is fine, but it is not spelled out.
Notation mixes additive and multiplicative ('0 → nG → G → G → 1'); harmless.

ideas.what: Injectivity of the section map X(K) → {sections of π1-extension}/conj, deduced from injectivity for the abelianized extension
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of Grothendieck's section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings, 1983); written proofs e.g. Nakamura, Stix (LNM 2054, 2013)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings, 27 June 1983 (published in Geometric Galois Actions I, 1997), where injectivity is asserted as known/easy

ideas.what: Comparison of the abelianized section class of a rational point with the Kummer class G(K) → lim H^1(K, nG), with the kernel being the divisible elements
ideas.modern_name: Kummer map / Tate-module Kummer theory for semi-abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Weil, Lang–Néron, Tate); in the section-conjecture context Stix and others

ideas.what: Reduction from elementary Artin neighbourhoods (fibres not P^1 or A^1) to subvarieties of semi-abelian varieties via a generalized Albanese
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian treatment of elementary neighbourhoods / Albanese reduction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings); Artin (SGA4 XI, for the neighbourhoods themselves)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 1983 (elementary neighbourhoods as anabelian varieties); SGA4 XI for the neighbourhoods

ideas.what: Remark (next page) that one needs all ℓ: the pro-ℓ version fails because of prime-to-ℓ torsion points (translation by a point of order p)
ideas.modern_name: Failure of injectivity of the pro-ℓ (ℓ-adic) section map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; discussed e.g. in Stix's work

missed.claim: This is an early, explicit hand-written proof of section-conjecture injectivity. It goes beyond curves to geometrically connected varieties embeddable in semi-abelian varieties, including elementary Artin neighbourhoods. It also notes in the margin a possible extension to positive characteristic for proper smooth X. The mathematics is standard and now well documented; the archival interest is in dating and attributing the injectivity argument to Grothendieck himself.
missed.quote: Il suffit de le prouver pour la seconde application, et on est ramené au cas où X est ... un groupe alg. ext. d'une VA par un tore
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution only: it confirms that Grothendieck had the Kummer/Mordell–Weil injectivity proof, in the semi-abelian generality, in the Longue Marche period.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard argument (Kummer theory plus Mordell–Weil) for the injectivity half of the section conjecture, already asserted by Grothendieck in the 1983 Faltings letter and proved in the literature. The semi-abelian/elementary-neighbourhood generality and the 'all ℓ' remark are known. It also contains a small slip: G(K) is not finitely generated when there is a torus part.
